..
Issued at 118 PM CST Tue Nov 3 2026

Early this afternoon, a deep, negatively tilted trough axis 
extends down the spine of the Plains. Along its leeward side, we
find a couple of distinct areas of low pressure, most notably 
one currently lifting northeast into NW MO, and an extensive 
baroclinic zone/warm conveyor impinging on the Midwest along and
ahead of the main surface cold front. Strong DCVA and quick 
upper height falls ahead of the deepening low make for a deeply 
dynamic system, especially upstream immediately east of the low 
level circulation. The storm also has plenty of layer moisture 
to work with as SPC mesoanalysis suggests between 1.5 and 1.7 
inches of PWAT resides over much of IL this afternoon. 
Resultantly, a large area of showers is lifting north-northeastward
roughly near and west of the I-55 corridor as of 1 PM.

These showers will gradually spread eastward and fill in the 
remainder of northern IL by early evening, although areas east 
of I-57 may stay largely dry well into the evening. The most 
widespread rainfall is expected around our CWA during the 
evening and overnight while the strongest forcing focuses over 
our area. Embedded pockets of heavy rain are expected and a few 
thunderstorms may be possible as well, primarily during the 
evening. A few hundred Joules of elevated CAPE are anticipated 
around our western CWA into this evening as the aforementioned 
low lifts into eastern IA. The deep forcing and moisture should 
allow parcels to make good use of that, but still should only 
support isolated chances for a couple of embedded storms through
the evening, mainly west of the Fox Valley. A big majority of 
deterministic camps paint at least localized stripes of near or 
over an inch of QPF through tonight. A few to several tenths is 
expected on a more widespread basis with the highest QPF largely
favored across the western half of the CWA. The better dynamics
will move away to the east by early tomorrow and take the 
higher shower coverage with. The surface cold front will move 
across the area during the day tomorrow and a few lighter 
showers may linger into tomorrow as it does, primarily through 
the morning. The latter half of Wednesday should be largely 
rain-free as a dry wedge advects in.

The southern flank of the vertically stacked low will park over
the general area late Wednesday into Thursday as the system 
gets hung up over the upper Midwest. This may drive some lighter
isolated showers mainly across our north Wednesday night into 
early Thursday. Chances increase again Thursday afternoon into 
early Friday as a secondary trough axis/cold front pivots 
across the region. High pressure then slides in bringing dry 
conditions to the weekend.

A strong low level wind field encompassing this storm will 
bring windy conditions to the next couple of days. The KLOT VWP 
as well as ACARS soundings out of Midway have been sampling 
around 45 to 50 kt of SSW flow down to 900mb since earlier this 
morning. At the surface, winds have regularly been gusting 
between 25 and 30 mph and as high as 35 mph at times. This will 
continue through mid-afternoon before easing slightly. Weak 
boundary layer static stability overnight with the stronger flow
remaining just off the deck will keep at least breezy 
conditions going through the night. The cold advection with the 
front moving across tomorrow should allow us to efficiently mix 
more 20 to 25 mph SW gusts down to the surface for the late 
morning and afternoon. And another breezy day is in store for 
Thursday with that secondary front pushing across.

Highs tomorrow are forecast to range from the upper 50s in our 
west to the middle and upper 60s into NW IN as the cooler 
airmass feeds in from the west. We won't be seeing much blue sky
over the next few days until the system ejects from the region 
late in the week. The coolest conditions over the next seven 
days are expected at the end of the week behind that secondary 
trough axis with daytime highs in the 50s Friday and Saturday 
and lows possibly getting down near freezing away from the city 
Friday and Saturday nights. A slight warmup is then favored for 
the early part of next week.

Doom
